title: EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION — register error labels; subsequent EXEC CICS auto-jump on the condition
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CICS-READ.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-REC    PIC X(80).
       01  WS-KEY    PIC X(10).
      *> EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION registers labels for runtime
      *> conditions. Subsequent EXEC CICS calls that raise NOTFND
      *> or NOTOPEN automatically jump to NOTFND-LABEL or NOTOPEN-LABEL
      *> -- the program does NOT inline a check. This is an
      *> exception-handler-like construct that is invisible in the
      *> straight-line code.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION
              NOTFND(NOTFND-LABEL)
              NOTOPEN(NOTOPEN-LABEL)
           END-EXEC.
           EXEC CICS READ FILE('POLICY')
              INTO(WS-REC) RIDFLD(WS-KEY)
           END-EXEC.
notes: HANDLE CONDITION is a particularly subtle CICS construct: the control flow it registers is OUT-OF-BAND from straight-line reads. A Java rewrite to try/catch is natural; the spec must capture every registered condition + target label so the rewrite's catches cover them.
